documents.title: Application Instructions for A Facility License (Section A forms; Section B supportive documents / plan of operation items)
documents.issuer: California Department of Social Services, Community Care Licensing Division (CCLD)
documents.version: The CDSS Forms I-L page lists LIC 281 (11/25) as the current edition. I could not open that PDF because cdss.ca.gov returned a permission error for the Portals URL. The item list below comes from the full LIC 281 (9/04) text, retrieved from the cdss.ca.gov /cdssweb/entres/forms/english/lic281.pdf URL. It matches the owner-supplied text. Compare it against the 11/25 PDF before submitting.
documents.url: https://www.cdss.ca.gov/Portals/9/Additional-Resources/Forms-and-Brochures/2020/I-L/LIC281.pdf?ver=cDy_GGClLQ7_6gtjxO-jNQ%3d%3d (current per CDSS forms list; 9/04 text read at https://www.cdss.ca.gov/cdssweb/entres/forms/english/lic281.pdf)
documents.how_used: The reviewer uses LIC 281 as the packet checklist. Section A lists the LIC forms. Section B lists the plan-of-operation documents and policies. Item numbers below are the document's own (A1-A16, B1-B17). The document uses bullets inside each B item, so sub-items are numbered here in bullet order (e.g., B7.1). Items for other facility types (A9.A, A17, B3, B18) are omitted.

required_items.text: LIC 200 - Application for a Community Care Facility or Residential Care Facility for the Elderly License. Form filled out completely; all applicants sign, including each general partner; original signatures only (no photocopied signatures); signatures match the applicant's name unless the applicant is a corporation or LLC; if a corporation applies, the Board resolution authorizing the signers must be submitted with the form.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section A table p.2; A1 p.3

required_items.text: LIC 215 - Applicant Information. One form completed by each applicant; original signatures; reference statements must be current and should not be from relatives.

LIC 308 - Designation of Facility (Administrative) Responsibility. At least one individual must be designated to act in the licensee's absence; a licensee cannot designate himself or herself; a corporation or LLC must submit a resolution authorizing the delegation; original signatures.

LIC 309 - Administrative Organization. Not required of individual applicants; required if the applicant is a corporation, public agency, partnership or LLC; information must match the LIC 200; terms of office should match articles/bylaws.
LIC 400 - Affidavit Regarding Client Cash Resources. Form completed with the appropriate box checked; make sure a bond is obtained if needed; original signatures.

LIC 402 - Surety Bond. Must use the LIC 402 language; State of California identified as beneficiary; effective and expiration dates; original seals and signatures; bond amount must match the amount on the LIC 400.

LIC 401 - Monthly Operating Statement. Number of clients corresponds to requested capacity; other facility income clear and documented; operating costs indicated and reasonable (salaries at least minimum wage); approximately 25 percent of salaries added for fringe benefits (or explain why not); rent matches lease/rental/mortgage payment; separate LIC 401 for each other licensed facility; indicate estimated or actual; preparer name and original signatures.

LIC 401a - Supplemental Financial Information. Part I (other income and expenses, excluding facility income) completed by individual applicants and each general partner; Part II completed by all applicants; preparer name and original signature.

LIC 403 - Balance Sheet. Complete the LIC 403a first; reflect assets and liabilities of all owner activities; figures must be 'realistic'; life insurance at cash/surrender value; real estate shown per applicant type; on-site furnishings and equipment at market value; only cash and cash equivalents count toward the three-month start-up funds; preparer name and original signatures.

LIC 403a - Balance Sheet Supplemental Schedule. Detailed balance sheet completed before the LIC 403; cash in the bank verified with the LIC 404; liabilities verified by credit report; preparer name and original signatures.

LIC 404 - Financial Information Release and Verification. Used to verify approximately three months of operating funds; a verifiable line of credit is acceptable if readily accessible; start-up funds should not be consumed on renovation or repair; the financial institution must send the verification directly to the licensing agency (the licensee cannot hand-carry it); one form or set per bank; all persons on an account sign; accounts in the applicant's name; original signatures.

LIC 500 - Personnel Report. Show all planned employee positions, with days and hours of duty (reviewed for required staff coverage for all hours of operation); list the Director/Administrator and any staff already hired; list unhired positions as 'to be hired' by position title; reverse side signed if there are fingerprint-exempt personnel; separate LIC 500 for each other licensed facility; original signatures.

LIC 501 - Personnel Record. Only for those who do not complete an LIC 215; submitted with the application only for directors/administrators who are not licensees; other staff forms are kept on file at the facility.

LIC 503 - Health Screening Report - Facility Personnel. One form each for the applicant or designee and the administrator; for RCFE applicants the screening must be less than six months old at the time of application; must be signed and dated by a qualified medical professional (no photocopied signatures); TB test portion completed including result, or separate test verification attached.
LIC 508 - Criminal Record Statement. One form each for the applicant or designee and the administrator.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section A table p.2; A13 p.9

required_items.text: LIC 610D (RCFE only: LIC 610E) - Emergency Disaster Plan. The plan must show two relocation sites away from the facility that can accommodate the number of residents; if the applicant does not currently occupy the property, use of the relocation site requires authorization from the agency or person in possession, verified in writing.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section A table p.2; A14 p.9

required_items.text: LIC 999 - Facility Sketch. Dimensions and use of all rooms; door and window exits shown, with exit routes indicated by number as on the LIC 610 Emergency Disaster Plan; rooms for non-ambulatory residents and staff identified; sketch of all indoor and outdoor space (driveways, fences, storage, gardens, recreation areas); separate sketches per building plus one overall sketch for multi-building sites; outdoor sketch shows dimensions, location of major equipment and swimming pools, and utility shut-off locations.
LIC 9054 - Fire Inspection. Listed as 'Required' for RCFE in the Section A table; no further instruction text appears for A16 in LIC 281.
Partnership Agreement / Articles of Incorporation / Articles of Organization. Required for RCFE; it tells the licensing agency who is ultimately responsible for which functions in the facility.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section B table p.10; B1 p.11

required_items.text: Partnership: a written agreement is not necessary when partners are husband and wife; two individuals not related by marriage must provide a partnership agreement.

Partnership: determine whether it is a general or limited partnership; for a limited partnership only the general partner(s) are on the license, but names and addresses of limited partners are also needed.
Partnership: all general partners need to be on the license and sign the application; name and business address of each general partner is needed.
Partnership: a description of the obligations and duties of each general partner and whether or not each can act on behalf of the others.

Articles of Incorporation: establish the applicant is a valid corporation qualified to do business in California; a seal from the state of incorporation should be attached; foreign (out-of-state) corporations must also provide a Certificate of Qualification from the California Secretary of State.
Corporation: constitution and by-laws (day-to-day operation).
Corporation: Board Resolution identifying the agents acting for the corporation, including authorization to apply for a license and the person authorized to sign and act on its behalf.
Corporation: directors' and officers' names, titles, business addresses and phone numbers; name and address of 10 percent shareholders.
Articles of Organization (LLC): stamped by the Secretary of State; a foreign LLC must also submit Secretary of State Form LLC-5 stamped by the California Secretary of State.

LLC: operating agreement; names, titles, business addresses and phone numbers of all managing members, managers, and non-managing members holding a 10 percent or more interest. If the signer is not identified in the operating agreement as having authority, a written delegation of authority consistent with the operating agreement is necessary.

Verification of Administrator Qualifications - For RCFE only: proof of registration in a 40-hour certification program submitted with the application; a Department-issued certificate verifying completion of the 40-hour RCFE certification program by an approved vendor is required prior to licensure.
Education: transcripts from an accredited school, when required; for out-of-country schools, class descriptions or college catalog, or certification of class equivalency from a local college.

Experience: written references obtained by the applicant/licensee and submitted (showing the person worked there, in what capacity, specific duties, and for what period); if references cannot be obtained, a declaration signed by the Administrator stating why and the same details.
Verification of experience for an applicant applying for a one to six bed ARF or RCFE is not necessary.

Job Descriptions - a job description for each staff classification; there must be a job description for each classification listed on the LIC 500, and staff positions must correspond to those listed on all personnel reports.
Each job description must address: duties and responsibilities.
Each job description must address: minimum qualifications that correspond to licensing requirements, including any special licenses, certificates or special skills needed for the job.
Each job description must address: lines of supervision (supervision given and to whom, and supervision received and from whom).
Personnel Policies - work hours/shifts documenting positions that provide coverage with competent staff, corresponding with the positions, work days and hours on all personnel reports.

Personnel Policies - abuse reporting procedures; documentation must indicate employees will be informed of their responsibilities to report to the licensing agency as well as to the police and child/adult protective agency.

Personnel Policies - hiring practices, including screening for necessary education and experience, and informing employees that conditions of employment include fingerprint clearance, statement of prior criminal convictions, TB clearance, physical examination/health questionnaire, and child abuse index check.

In-Service Training for Staff - a plan for in-service training submitted at the time of application, as part of the plan of operation. New employee training: a description of the training and who will conduct it.

Ongoing training: topics to be covered (the list should include administrator continuing education units); how often the training will be given; how the training will be documented; must include topics specified in the regulation sections listed (for RCFE: 87565 Residential Care Facilities for the Elderly Regulations; 80065 General Regulations also listed).
Program Description (CCF/RCFE) - brief statement of the purpose, goals and program methods (program philosophy). A pamphlet or brochure is acceptable if all of the elements B7.1-B7.11 are included.
Days and hours of operation.
Daily schedule of activities provided by the facility, stating who plans, conducts and assists clients in participating.
A one month schedule of planned social, educational and recreational activities, stating who plans, conducts and assists clients in participating.
Description of the basic services provided by the facility (see Admission Guideline LIC 604 or 604A for a list of basic services).
Description of the optional services provided in the facility as listed in the admission agreement.
Description of how the facility will handle medical emergencies if a client becomes ill or injured.
Procedure for handling and assisting clients/residents with self-administered medications.
Transportation arrangements.
Description of community resources and consultants to be used by the facility.
A procedure (approved by the licensing agency) for immediate response to incidents and complaints.

Rules of Discipline / Personal Rights (titled 'Discipline Policies' in the text) - personal rights applies to all facility categories. The detailed discipline-policy content in the document is for group homes and foster family agencies only.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section B table p.10; B8 p.17

required_items.text: The Department evaluates the discipline policies to ensure they do not violate personal rights and that there is a clear statement that no corporal or unusual punishment will be used; further information may be requested if the statements are unclear.

Admission Policies - persons accepted for care, including age range and compatibility determination process, when necessary. Overall, the policies must provide ages of clients, rates and refund policies, acceptance and retention limitations, pre-admission appraisals, needs and services plans, medical assessments, and an admission agreement.
Intake procedures for placement in group homes (listed in the document's B9 list; it names group homes only).
Criteria for assessing appropriateness of placement given an individual client's needs (interviews, procedures for obtaining and developing the necessary paperwork, etc.).
Needs and services plan.
Client's Rights/Personal Rights (at a minimum a statement that residents will be informed of their rights and that their rights will not be violated).
Medical assessment.
Pre-admission appraisal plan.
Emergency information.
Sign-in and sign-out procedures.
Immunization requirements.
Physical examination requirements (including TB testing).
Sample Menu - planned meals and snacks for one week, with foods from the four basic food groups.
Sample Menu - portion sizes.
Sample Menu - times meals served.
Control of Property - name and address of the owner of the property.

Control of Property - a copy of the lease or rental agreement (no requirement on length). If the agreement precludes use as a facility or operation is contrary to its terms, the license must be denied/withdrawn.
Control of Property - proof of ownership if the applicant owns the property (property tax bill, deed or other document containing the facility street address).

Bacterial Analysis of Water - only if the facility gets water from a well or other private source (required at initial licensure regardless of number of clients): evidence of on-site inspection of the source and a bacteriological analysis by a local or state health department or other qualified laboratory establishing the water is safe; analysis signed by a qualified agency representative.

Insurance Information (RCFE only) - a statement on whether there will be insurance covering the facility operation; if so, the type of coverage and with whom; if none, a statement of such is sufficient.

Theft and Loss Policy (RCFE only) - must include provisions for inventory of personal property at admission, modification of the inventory, practices to safeguard personal property upon the death of the resident, documentation and reporting of loss of personal property, method of marking personal property, and method for providing a secure area for safekeeping of resident personal property.

Neighborhood Complaint Policy - procedures for immediate response to incidents and complaints, including a time when the owner, licensee or designee will be available to meet with neighborhood residents. The text says it is applicable to non-resident owner community care facilities providing care for six or fewer persons only; the Section B table marks it 'Required' in the RCFE column.
required_items.cite: LIC 281, Section B table p.10; B15 p.20

required_items.text: First Aid Card - staff providing direct care and supervision must receive first aid training from qualified persons (e.g., American Red Cross); copies of first aid cards for applicant/administrators must be submitted and will be verified.
Orientation Certificate - proof of attendance must be submitted with the application.
Final checklist: Have you attended an orientation for your facility type and submitted a copy of your orientation certificate(s)?
Final checklist: Is your application (LIC 200) signed and dated by all applicants?
Final checklist: Do you have an Emergency Disaster Plan (LIC 610)?
Final checklist: Do you have a Facility Sketch (LIC 999) showing indoor/outdoor space as well as all exits?
Final checklist: Have you completed all Financial Information to operate your facility?
Final checklist: Have you enclosed your application fee?
Final checklist: Be sure all necessary information is completed, properly signed (original signature) and dated.

sections: Section A - Forms by Type of Facility (A1-A16 for RCFE)
Section B - Supportive Documents (B1, B2, B4-B17 for RCFE; B3 and B18 do not apply)
Final checklist ('Have you remembered the following')

notes: LIC 281 has no single 'plan of operation' form. The application fee plus Section A and Section B documents go to the licensing agency as one packet. Per LIC 281, submit them in the same sequence as the booklet. An incomplete packet is returned in full. All forms need original signatures and dates, and the applicant should keep a photocopy. The reviewer compares documents against each other: job descriptions (B4) must match the LIC 500; work hours in the personnel policies (B5) must match the personnel reports; and the exit routes on the LIC 999 must match the LIC 610 plan. Organize the manual by B-number in this order: B1, B2, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8, B9, B10, B11, B12 (only if the water supply is private), B13, B14, B15, B16, B17. B15 (neighborhood complaint policy) is marked 'Required' for RCFE in the table, but the B15 text limits it to non-resident-owner facilities of six or fewer. B9 includes a group-home intake bullet, and B8's discipline detail is for group homes and FFAs only. B7 says its '**' items may also appear in 'Section B10 - Admission Policies'; the document most likely means B9. Newer program-specific plan-of-operation content, such as the infection control plan and the dementia and hospice waivers listed in your regulations, is not in LIC 281. Use the Title 22 sections you listed (87208 plan of operation and others) as supplements. The CDSS forms page lists the current edition as LIC 281 (11/25), which I could not retrieve, so confirm the numbering against it before filing.
